column1: # The constructs that are written only in this compiler's language, one per row:
#     <feature>
# The reference compiler (the pinned bootstrap) lacks the user-approved features this compiler alone
# has, so it refuses to PARSE a block written with one, and the emit-ast sweep over the reference pages
# (tests_oracle.sysl, the_two_agree_on_the_reference_pages) would call every such block a divergence.
# **The rule for that sweep**: a block the reference refuses is excused only where this compiler's own
# lexer finds one of these constructs in its tokens -- never by page or block number, which moves
# whenever a page is edited -- AND this compiler either reads the block or refuses it in words quoting
# one of the construct's words ('async', 'const': a page showing the feature's own refusal). A block
# this compiler refuses for anything else is compared as before. An excused block is counted and named
# in SYSL_ORACLE_SUMMARY; every other divergence is still a failure.
# A construct is a run of tokens separated by spaces. A word matches a keyword, an operator or a name of
# that spelling; <name> matches any name; <fixed-type> a fixed-point type's name (iWqF, uWqF, q7, q15,
# q31); <fixed-literal> a number carrying a fixed-point suffix (0.5i32q31); <counted-spec> an f"..."
# literal one of whose specifiers takes its width or precision from a hole (${x}%.${n}f); <newline> and
# <indent> the layout's line end and indent, so a construct may name where a block begins. Text inside a
# comment or a string is never a token, so mentioning a feature does not excuse a block.
# **<counted-spec> is the one construct the reference PARSES** -- as ordinary text and a hole -- so a
# block written in it is excused whichever way either compiler answers, not only where the reference
# refuses it.
# Only the features with a SYNTAX of their own are here, since the sweep compares parse trees: run-time
# skip, infinity/nan, slot_storage/slot_place/slot_vacate and Task[T] are spelled as ordinary names,
# calls and types the reference parses; nounwind, sysl prove, LTO/PGO, the bounds message and
# workspaces are not written in a block at all.
